abstract.para: &kexec; starts a new kernel directly from the running kernel, without going through the firmware and the boot loader. A reboot with &kexec; is therefore faster than a normal reboot.

topic.para: The kexec command from the kexec-tools package loads the new kernel into memory through the kexec system call. The running kernel then hands control to the new kernel.

listitem.para: Faster reboots. Skipping the firmware and the boot loader saves time, which matters if you reboot a system often, for example after kernel updates.
Booting another kernel once. You can load any kernel image with the kernel options you choose, without changing the boot loader configuration.

section.title: When to use a full reboot
section.para: Use a full reboot when you need the firmware or the boot loader to run:

listitem.para: Firmware updates. Changes to the firmware take effect only when the firmware runs during a full reboot.
Selecting an entry in the boot menu. A &kexec; reboot does not show the boot menu, so you cannot select another boot entry or an older snapshot there.
Devices that do not work after a &kexec; reboot. A full reboot lets the firmware reset and initialize the hardware.

section.para: If a kernel is already loaded for &kexec;, unload it before a full reboot. Otherwise, systemctl reboot also reboots with &kexec;. See .
